{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -J RNAseq
#   -o logs/snakemake_%J.out
#   -e logs/snakemake_%J.err
#   -R "select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4]"
#   -q rna

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --queue=rna \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs

# Approximate LSF %J with Flux job id.
exec >"logs/snakemake_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"logs/snakemake_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: LSF memory constraint (-R select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4]) has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J RNAseq) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

module load singularity/3.9.2

# NOTE: This workflow uses Snakemake --drmaa with LSF-specific bsub options in the DRMAA string.
# There is no universally portable way to translate this cluster-submission layer to Flux within this script.
# Performance implication: per-rule resource requests and scheduling will not be handled by Flux as intended;
# jobs may oversubscribe/underutilize resources or fail to submit.

args=' 
  -q rna 
  -o {log}.out 
  -e {log}.err 
  -J {params.job_name} 
  -R "{params.memory} span[hosts=1] " 
  -n {threads} '

snakemake \
    --drmaa "$args" \
    --snakefile Snakefile \
    --configfile config.yaml \
    --jobs 12 \
    --latency-wait 60 \
    --rerun-incomplete \
    --use-singularity \
    --singularity-args "--bind /beevol/home/rbilab --bind /beevol/home/wellskri --bind /beevol/home/wellskri/packages/bin --bind /tmp:/tmp"
'

# Notes on omitted translations:
# - No LSF walltime/CPU count was specified beyond the Snakemake/DRMAA layer, so the Flux allocation uses defaults.
#   Performance implication: defaults may be insufficient for the pipeline controller process.
"
}
